Paragraph: When Romapada agreed Dasaratha's tormented mind raced with joy. Free of all anxiety, he approached Rshyasringa, reverently with folded palms. He said that bereft of sons, he wished to perform suitable rituals to beget children and that Rshyasringa should preside over them and bless him with sons. His boons were granted. Four sons of great renown were born, bringing glory and fame to the Ikshvakus unequaled in all the three worlds. This was the story told by Sanath Kumara during the early period of Krita Yuga.
Chapter/Canto/Verse_Reference: Bala Kanda, Chapter 14 (Conclusion of the Rishyasringa Episode and Birth of Rama's Brothers)
Situation/Problem_Faced: Dasaratha's longstanding problem of childlessness is finally addressed. With Rishyasringa present (after Romapada's approval), the conditions are met for the performance of the ritual to beget sons.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: This passage highlights the culmination of faith, perseverance, and the efficacy of spiritual rituals and the blessings of righteous ascetics. It emphasizes that profound desires, when pursued with appropriate means and spiritual support, can be fulfilled. The divine intervention and the birth of the four sons underscore the concept of boons and their transformative power.
Outcome/Resolution: Dasaratha's long-held wish for progeny is granted. Rishyasringa presides over the necessary rituals, leading to the birth of four illustrious sons (Rama, Lakshmana, Bharata, and Shatrughna), bringing immense joy and glory to the Ikshvaku dynasty. The drought in Angada is also implicitly resolved through Rishyasringa's presence earlier.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.anxiety: Peace of Mind, Stress Reduction, Calmness

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: The narrative culminates in the spiritual fulfillment of Dasaratha's deepest Kama (desire) through the successful performance of sacred rituals, presided over by a powerful ascetic like Rishyasringa. The birth of the four sons is presented as a direct Phala (fruit/result) of these spiritual efforts and the Asheervada (blessing) of the sages and divine. It reinforces the belief in the efficacy of prayer and yajnas to bring about desired outcomes, aligning with divine will.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Psychologically, this passage depicts a profound shift from long-standing anxiety and torment to overwhelming joy and relief for Dasaratha. The successful outcome of his pursuit of progeny brings a deep sense of fulfillment and achievement. This serves as a powerful example of how the resolution of a major life concern, especially one tied to identity and legacy, can dramatically improve psychological well-being, replacing distress with happiness and a renewed sense of hope and optimism.
